localities.name: Kolathur
localities.plot_band_note: IMPORTANT - the roofandfloor Kolathur plot page is heavily padded with listings that are NOT in North-Chennai Kolathur. I dropped seven of its ten rows (GTK Eutopia Smart City 2,793, New Star City 2,899, Om Lakshmi Nagar Annex 2,700, Aishwaryam Township 2,500, i5 CK Madhavan Nagar 1,932-3,200, RWD Elite Avenue 4,798, Premier KVT Township 5,100) because they sit 2-4x below the verified Kolathur land field - these are almost certainly outer-belt layouts (there is a second Kolathur near Tiruvallur) surfaced as 'nearby'. I also dropped Silversky Springs, quoted at 15,483/sqft: recomputing gives 1.2Cr/775 = 15,484 but 1.44Cr/1,447 = 9,952, i.e. internally inconsistent, which means the price includes BUILT villa area, not raw land. That is exactly the outlier pattern to reject. What survives is a tight, internally consistent field: two named layouts plus four search-visible vacant-plot rates, spanning 8,530-10,499 - reported as the band since n=6 is too thin to trim further.
localities.price_band_note: Apartment BUILT-UP rate. Apartment rates read 7,000-11,000/sqft with an average of 8,050/sqft (Aug 2026), up from ~7,700/sqft in Apr 2026; independent houses command 9,000-13,000/sqft. I trimmed the 11,000 top edge to 10,000 as it reflects a handful of new premium launches rather than the body of the market. Note we track 7 plot projects and ZERO apartment projects here, yet the apartment resale market is the dominant product - a coverage gap worth closing.
localities.band_audit: The existing band 6,500-8,500 is a genuine APARTMENT BUILT-UP rate, correctly labelled, but it is now stale - apartments moved +12.6% YoY and the current field is 7,000-10,000. Separately, be aware that in Kolathur LAND (8,500-10,500) trades ABOVE built-up (7,000-10,000). That inversion is normal for a dense, fully built-out inner locality where land is the scarce input, and it is the opposite of the outer-belt localities in this set where land is roughly half of built-up. Do not 'correct' it.
localities.trend_note: Apartments +12.6% YoY with the broader locality appreciating 7-9% annually on Inner Ring Road commercial growth, storm-water drainage upgrades and Madhavaram metro-hub proximity.

localities.name: Thoraipakkam

localities.name: Mangadu
localities.plot_band_note: Unusually tight and mutually confirming. All three named Mangadu layouts recompute to essentially the same rate: VLC Karikala Cholan Nagar 39.99L/800 = 4,999; Thiya Garden 39.99L/800 = 4,999; Nu Tech Samruddhi 50.4L/1,008 = 5,000. An IQR of three identical values is degenerate, so I widened to the independently reported 99acres land range of 4,550-5,600, which brackets the layouts symmetrically. TRAP CAUGHT: chennaiproperties lists a Kovur parcel at a quoted '80,000/sqft' - recomputing 1.6Cr/2,000 gives 8,000/sqft, a 10x error in the source's own per-sqft field, and it is Kovur not Mangadu. Dropped on both grounds. Only 2 plot projects tracked here versus 71 in neighbouring Kundrathur, so Mangadu is a much smaller land market at a ~50% higher rate.
localities.price_band_note: Apartment BUILT-UP rate, unchanged and re-verified: 99acres range 5,250-7,850/sqft, average 6,450/sqft. 1BHK 19.9L-49.03L, 2BHK 44.85L-72.3L. 71+ apartments listed, so a genuine resale/low-rise apartment market exists even though we track zero RERA apartment projects here - a coverage gap, not an absence of market.
localities.band_audit: The cleanest of the existing records. The band 5,250-7,850 is a genuine APARTMENT BUILT-UP rate, correctly labelled, and still current. Its note already separated the plotted-land rate (4,550-5,600/sqft) rather than conflating the two, and my three named layouts land at ~5,000/sqft, right inside that range. No correction needed - only promotion of the land figure out of the note and into a proper plot band.
localities.trend_note: Slower and steadier than neighbouring Kundrathur - flats +7.5% in 1 year (vs +27.5% at Kundrathur), +24.0% in 3 years - on Porur IT spillover and the Poonamallee metro terminus ~4 km north.

localities.name: Siruvanur
localities.plot_band_note: NO USABLE DATA - and I believe the locality itself is mis-assigned rather than merely under-covered. Nothing named 'Siruvanur' surfaces as a Chennai Metropolitan Area locality on any portal, hyperlocal site or search. Two observations, offered as leads rather than conclusions: (1) the two projects we track here (Sri Balaji Avenue Phase II, Phase III) carry RERA numbers TNRERA-2-LO-4118-2025 and TNRERA-2-LO-4161-2025 - district segment '2' - whereas the Chembarambakkam layout in the same dataset carries TNRERA-29-LO-4000-2025. Different district segment, which is at least consistent with these projects not being in the Chennai district group; I could not verify the TNRERA district code table, so this is suggestive only. (2) The closest real-world name match is SIRUGANUR, on the Trichy-Chennai NH in Tiruchirappalli district, ~300 km outside the CMA, where DTCP land trades at roughly Rs 250-942/sqft - an order of magnitude below any CMA rate. Searches also surfaced Siruvallur (a Perambur neighbourhood in North Chennai, not 'Far West'), Siruvalur (Ariyalur) and Siruvachur (Perambalur), none of which fit. RECOMMENDATION: pull the source RERA filings for those two projects and confirm the village/taluk/district before publishing any band. If they are Trichy-district layouts they should be dropped from the CMA dataset, not priced. I have deliberately returned no band rather than borrow a neighbour's rate.

localities.name: Chengalpattu town
localities.plot_band_note: Interquartile range of 31 named plotted layouts (n=31, median ~Rs 1,350/sqft), every rate recomputed by me as min_price/min_size and cross-checked against max_price/max_size. Dropped 4 outliers: Nammazhvar Organic (Rs 198/sqft, 9,582-43,556 sqft organic FARMLAND), The Country Village Farmland (Rs 299/sqft, 10,000 sqft farmland), Red Sandal (Rs 110/sqft, 9,200 sqft agricultural parcel) - all bulk agri land, not residential plots - and Lake View (Madurantakam Main Road, ~30km outside town). Also excluded a 6-acre bulk parcel at Rs 2.52 Cr that recomputes to Rs 96/sqft (raw agricultural aggregation). CAUTION: most portals conflate Chengalpattu TOWN with Chengalpattu DISTRICT - the generic 'chengalpattu' slug returns Thiruporur/Kelambakkam/Singaperumal Koil stock at 3-5x town rates. The working slug is 'chengalpet', not 'chengalpattu'. Corroborated by independent recomputed points: Chengalpattu 600sqft @ Rs 7.5L = Rs 1,250/sqft, Mamandur 1200sqft @ Rs 14.81L = Rs 1,234/sqft, Kayar 800sqft @ Rs 16L = Rs 2,000/sqft, plus search-snippet figures of Rs 1,800/sqft (Chengalpattu Township), Rs 1,750/sqft (Kanchipuram-Chengalpattu Rd), Rs 2,500/sqft (Kanchipuram High Rd nr SRK Cinemas), Rs 714/sqft (Mamandur), Rs 650/sqft (I5 Global City) - all inside or adjacent to the band.
localities.price_band_note: Apartment BUILT-UP asking rates. IQR of 9 credible points: Mahindra Nova 3,500; Mahindra Iris Court 4,050; NoBroker Dec-2025 4,300; NoBroker Jul-2026 5,727; Mahindra Lakewoods 6,144; Under-construction (Square Yards) 6,150; Mahindra World City 6,153; Square Yards Mar-2026 asking 6,588; Square Yards Jun-2026 apartment 6,600. Villa product sits higher at 8,400/sqft and is excluded - it is built villa, not comparable to flat built-up. Note land here is roughly ONE FIFTH of built-up rate, the widest land-to-built-up gap in this set.
localities.trend_note: Apartments flat at 0% YoY and under-construction stock DOWN 4.23% (Square Yards Jun-2026); heavy plotted-layout supply (104 RERA plot registrations tracked) is capping land appreciation, though Mahindra World City and the Siemens Gamesa industrial anchor support the floor. Villas alone show +27.87%.
localities.band_audit: The existing band [4500, 6600] genuinely measures APARTMENT BUILT-UP asking rates - it is correctly labelled and its note already flags the Square Yards asking-price skew. It is NOT contaminated by land. Its only defect was the absence of any plot band, which matters enormously here: 104 of 111 tracked projects are plotted layouts, and land trades at Rs 750-2,300/sqft, about a quarter of the apartment number. Anyone applying the 4,500-6,600 band to a plot deal would overprice land by roughly 4x. My band nudges the floor down to 4,200 to reflect Mahindra Iris Court/Nova entry stock and the NoBroker Dec-2025 reading.

localities.name: Velachery
localities.plot_band_note: THIN - only 2 plot projects tracked and Velachery has almost no remaining raw land, so this rests on 4 recomputed resale points plus a portal range. Recomputed: MGP Aditri II 2,400sqft @ Rs 1.98Cr = Rs 8,250/sqft; 1,800sqft CMDA @ Rs 1.85Cr = Rs 10,278/sqft; 1,200sqft (Mar-2026) @ Rs 2.2Cr = Rs 18,333/sqft. DROPPED two: a 1,200sqft @ Rs 70L listing recomputing to Rs 5,833/sqft, which is BELOW the Rs 9,294/sqft circle rate and therefore cannot be a genuine registrable Velachery transaction (stale or mislabelled), and the Rs 18,333/sqft point as a single premium/metro-frontage outlier. Floor anchored on the published circle rate (Rs 9,294/sqft, hexahome 2026); ceiling on the 99acres land range of Rs 10,350-14,050/sqft. Treat as indicative, not transactional.
localities.price_band_note: Apartment BUILT-UP. 99acres flat range Rs 7,300-11,600/sqft with average ~Rs 9,400; reported average TRANSACTION rate Rs 10,164/sqft; another source cites Rs 9,500 average. Luxury projects quoted above Rs 15,000/sqft are excluded as a separate premium tier, not mid-market comparables.
localities.trend_note: Mature, fully built-out market with negligible new land supply; asking rates flat year-on-year and a transacted average (Rs 10,164) sitting close to the asking midpoint, which signals a liquid but not appreciating market.
localities.band_audit: The existing band [7850, 13250] measures APARTMENT BUILT-UP and is correctly labelled - the note's ~Rs 9,500 average matches the 99acres and transaction figures. However its Rs 13,250 ceiling is luxury-skewed: the mainstream 99acres flat range tops out at Rs 11,600, and 13,250 sits inside the LAND band (9,300-13,500) rather than the mid-market flat band. Anyone reading 13,250 as a normal Velachery flat rate would overpay. I have tightened the apartment band to 8,200-11,600 and split the land rate out separately.

localities.name: Adambakkam
localities.plot_band_note: Land rate per sqft. Portal land range Rs 11,400-15,000/sqft (99acres), corroborated by the one clean recomputed comparable I could verify: 900 sqft at Rs 1.08 Cr near Puzhuthivakkam MRTS = Rs 12,000/sqft exactly. Only 4 plot projects tracked and genuine vacant land is scarce here, so comparables are few. I DISCARDED a widely-syndicated 3,132 sqft @ Rs 1.85 Cr listing (recomputes to Rs 5,907/sqft) as inconsistent with every other Adambakkam land observation and likely a mis-scraped record. NOTE the land band sits ABOVE the apartment band here - normal for a built-out inner suburb where a redevelopable plot carries FSI value.
localities.price_band_note: Apartment BUILT-UP. 99acres flat range Rs 8,550-10,900/sqft, average ~Rs 9,000; weighted average cited at Rs 10,000/sqft.
localities.trend_note: Land rates up 29.2% year-on-year against flats up only 2.9% (99acres) - a classic redevelopment-driven land squeeze, with Metro Phase 2 alignment through the Adambakkam/Puzhuthivakkam corridor pulling plot values ahead of built stock.
localities.band_audit: The existing band [8500, 12200] is labelled apartment and its floor (8,500) is a sound apartment built-up figure matching the 99acres 8,550 low. But the band is a MIX, not a clean apartment band: its Rs 12,200 ceiling exceeds the mainstream flat range (which tops at 10,900) and sits squarely inside the LAND band (11,400-15,000). The note's own reference to 'NoBroker premium pockets up to Rs 19,400' is almost certainly a land or ultra-premium figure, not mid-market flat built-up. So the upper half of the existing band is land/premium contamination and should not be used to price a flat.

localities.name: Anumanthaputheri
localities.plot_band_note: NO USABLE MARKET BAND FOUND - deliberately returning found:false rather than a fabricated figure. What I did establish: Anumanthaputheri is a revenue village in CHENGALPATTU taluk (Chengalpattu district), not the Kanchipuram corridor as currently tagged in the dataset - worth correcting. The tnlandlord.in village page for it exists but renders navigation only, with no prices. The ONLY price-like figure anywhere is a third-party guideline-value mirror quoting Rs 1,650/sqft for 'Anumanthaputheri Nadu Street' dated 2024, and per the brief a GV from a stale third-party mirror is weak corroboration only, never a market rate. Notably it CONTRADICTS the 2-3x-GV heuristic here: 2x of 1,650 would imply ~Rs 3,300/sqft, far above the Rs 750-2,300 band I measured across 31 real Chengalpattu-town layouts, so the mirror is likely stale or mis-keyed. No portal slug exists (roofandfloor, chennaiproperties, sulekha, nestoria all return nothing for this village). The three tracked projects are all registry-only plotted layouts (NS Nagar Virivu I/II/III by K. Nithiyanandam) with no pricing. NEAREST DEFENSIBLE PROXY, to be used only as context and NOT written in as this locality's band: the Chengalpattu-town layout belt at Rs 750-2,300/sqft.
localities.price_band_note: No apartment market - zero apartment projects tracked and none found in research. Correctly null; the land proxy must NOT be copied across.

localities.name: Vengambakkam
localities.plot_band_note: IQR of 5 recomputed comparables (median Rs 4,800/sqft). Rates recomputed by me: Dollars Colony Phase 2 Rs 40.57L/712 = Rs 5,698; Grand Avenue Rs 50L/1,200 = Rs 4,167 rising to Rs 1.24Cr/2,400 = Rs 5,167 (this one is NOT a flat marketing rate, so I carried both ends); individual 3,750sqft plot Rs 1.8Cr = Rs 4,800; Maxworth Zion 150 Rs 44.25L/924 = Rs 4,789. NOTE the dataset tags this GST Road, but Vengambakkam actually sits on the Vandalur-Kelambakkam road near Mappedu/Rathinamangalam - worth checking the corridor label.
localities.price_band_note: Apartment BUILT-UP, THIN - only 1 apartment project tracked. Anchored on the 99acres weighted average of Rs 5,550/sqft for Vengambakkam, plus the one curated project: Casagrand Estia, which I recomputed from its own price/size ranges as Rs 52L/1,076 = Rs 4,833 to Rs 72L/1,589 = Rs 4,531 per sqft. Land and built-up sit unusually close here, which is genuine for an inner-periphery node with expensive land and modest built product, not contamination.
localities.trend_note: Apartment prices up 11.0% in the last year (99acres) on Vandalur-Kelambakkam road widening and OMR/GST cross-connectivity; plotted supply is still absorbing at Rs 4,800-5,700.

localities.name: Orikkai

That inversion is unusual and important: the general rule that Chennai land trades at a third of built-up does not hold here, because Medavakkam's remaining plotted supply is scarce, junction-adjacent and metro-facing while its apartment stock is mid-market builder product. Anyone applying a land-vs-flat ratio heuristic to this locality will get it badly wrong.
